classification: prepared and independently reviewed; physical warm boots unperformed

result.scope: Focused independent re-review of preservation-admission fix, associated tests and documentation; original blocked report retained unchanged.
result.original_blocker: Resolved: nested unit/journal/dmesg command captures, all six RAM-file captures and readable UART retention are validated before any probe or reboot. The prior all-failed nested-capture reproduction now refuses before transport.
findings: capture_bytes requires exact integer zero returncode, explicit false timeout/truncation flags, strict base64 and byte bounds. Journals require consistent record counts and no possible truncation.

preserved_snapshot requires all expected unit identities and stopped guest/CPU/observer state with numeric exit fields; nonzero workload exit status remains admissible because this gate verifies retention rather than endurance success.
All six native FILES records must exist, have distinct expected paths and consistent captured extents. Empty complete CPU output and stderr are allowed. Small observer/CPU files must be complete.

Actual observer sources scripts/observe-endurance-kvm-exit.py and scripts/observe-first-kvm-exit.py use event=ready/event=final with unit=a733-guest-endurance.service as expected. Failed observer outcomes retain ready plus stderr, which the new gate deliberately admits.
Native preserver show() emits Id and exit properties for the same five units; remote_snapshot emits files, units, guest/kernel/manager journals and dmesg with the fields expected by the new guards.

Management-watch JSONL may retain a consistent tail; its first potentially partial line is skipped and later complete object records are required. UART may use a consistent nonempty tail or a readable nonempty regular native archive. These exceptions do not admit incomplete CPU or observer files.

No change was made to the previously reviewed zero-transport default, fixed-target SSH/identity checks, namespace proof, idle-workload guards, clean ten-request loop, distinct canonical boot ID handling or failure evidence retention.
